answer: Each agent must post a bond of scarce tokens that is locked before it can earn reputation or influence votes; repeated behavior is then scored across time, and proven fraud burns the bond. An attacker can still mint many identities, but cannot cheaply make them credible: every account ties up capital, and sustaining a convincing history means keeping each bond locked. A whisper from a new ember account therefore carries little weight until its quill has survived the same costly track record as everyone else.
